posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

Does the Skydeck thingy say "When a target would be destroyed, put it to the bottom of its deck instead"? Because if so, that's a bit like Unforgiving Wasteland's "When a target would be destroyed (by the environment), remove it from the game instead" which lets you get around stuff like Lilian's Fowl-destruction damage. But I suppose if it says "when a target is destroyed…" (as opposed to "would be destroyed"), then it still does its normal destruction stuff, just goes to the bottom of the deck afterwards rather than the trash.

Unfortunately, now that I've read it, it provides no such clarification.  It can't ever work on One-Shots, of course, since those aren't "destroyed" but simply "put into trash".  But if we pretend that it could be in play at the same time as Imbued Vitality, then all other cards would be targets and thus would be Skydecked "when destroyed", which seems to imply that they are still indeed destroyed.  But I still wish it had been written with "instead of into the trash" for clarity's sake, and for that matter that it had said "on the bottom of that deck" instead of "underneath that deck" (which implies that there's some Dreamer-esque limbo zone underneath the deck, which wouldn't count as part of the deck itself).  Especially given that Parse and Writhe have cards which mess with the bottom cards of decks, and the use of different language on Skydeck seems to indicate a distinction, one that'd be meant to prevent Writhe from Extracting a Skydecked target, but probably doesn't actually exist.

Would it be possible for someone who playtested for Vengeance to shed some light on this weirdness?

posts.name: Edwin
posts.cooked:
lynkfox:

Or, err ont he side of the players.

See, I would say err against the side of the players; victory in a coop game means nothing if the game-loss condition (the villain in SOTM) doesn't pose a substantial threat.  Arkham Horror is just about the ideal coop game because you almost always lose, so finally beating Cthulhu proves that you've really accomplished something.  SOTM is much more enjoyable in the process than Arkham (not to mention quicker), but the outcome can be a bit of a foregone conclusion except against the very toughest villains (about a third or so).  More than half the time, not even one hero goes down, which makes me think perhaps SOTM as a whole (again, with exceptions for the likes of Chairman and Capitan) is excessively easy, so its bragging rights aren't worth all that much.  Ever being generous to players in rules calls would exacerbate that effect, though of course it might be worth it, if the stakes are whether a player is having fun.  So if someone feels like Ra is useless, and then they get out Solar Flare and Flesh of the Sun God and now they think he's awesome, maybe it's acceptible not to point out Ruling 15 to them and have them go back to feeling lame.  But it means that your victory in that game doesn't entirely "count" either, and likewise if you legitimately don't know what to do, but you rule in your own favor and that ends up giving you the win.
